tip: dürfen with keine means forbidden, not 'don't have to': 'dürfen keine Pflanzen pflücken' = are not allowed to pick any plants.
In a passive, 'by' the doer is von, not bei: 'von der Personalabteilung geprüft' = reviewed by HR. bei would mean 'at'.
an is two-way: staying put takes dative, 'an der Wand' where the picture just hangs there; moving onto it would flip to accusative die Wand.
'hätte gern besucht' is counterfactual past: she would have liked to attend but did not. Not politeness here, a thing that never happened.
ein shows no gender, so the adjective carries it: 'ein kalter Wind', where kalter takes the -er that der would have shown.
wolle is Konjunktiv I, the reported-speech form: 'sie sagte, sie wolle auswandern' = she said she wanted to emigrate.
Negate a possessive with nicht, never kein: 'nicht mein Koffer' = not my suitcase. kein is only for nouns with no article.
German makes being glad reflexive: 'ich freue mich' literally I gladden myself, while English just says I'm happy.
When something other than the subject opens, the verb stays second: 'Heute ist es kälter' puts ist before the subject es.
ob means whether and sends the verb to the end: 'ob das Geschäft sonntags geöffnet ist' closes with ist.
The formal command keeps Sie right after the verb, same order as a question: 'Schalten Sie bitte...' = please switch.
Use als for 'than' in comparisons: 'fließender als' = more fluently than. wie is only for 'as...as' equality.
With a reflexive pronoun, 'sich verstehen' means get along, not understand: 'wir verstehen uns gut' = we get along well.
The du-command is the verb stem with no du and no -st: from du sagst you get 'Sag Bescheid' = let me know.
halten für, literally 'hold for', means consider or regard as: 'ich halte es für wichtig' = I consider it important.
über meaning 'about' a topic takes the accusative: 'über meine Pläne' = about my plans. No motion here, just the subject matter.
Fear uses a fixed frame, Angst haben vor plus the dative: 'Angst vor Spinnen' = afraid of spiders.
'Guten Morgen' is accusative because it is a leftover of '(ich wünsche) einen guten Morgen', I wish you a good morning.
als is 'when' for one finished past event, while wenn is for repeated ones: 'als wir die gute Nachricht erhalten haben' ends with the verb.
sich treffen mit needs the reflexive dich: 'du dich mit Freunden triffst' = you meet up with friends. Drop dich and treffen means to hit or run into.
deren means 'whose', the possessive relative word: 'die Lehrerin, deren Unterricht...' = the teacher whose lessons...
In a dass-clause the conjugated verb moves to the very end: 'dass du kommen konntest' closes with konntest.
Unlike English 'although', obwohl sends the verb to the very end: 'obwohl es draußen regnet' finishes with regnet.
German builds the passive with werden, not sein: 'wird das Essen frisch zubereitet' = the food is prepared fresh.
wegen means 'because of' and takes the genitive: 'wegen des Staus' = because of the traffic jam. Spoken German often slips to dative.
warten auf takes the accusative, so the relative word is 'auf den', not auf dem: 'der Zug, auf den wir warten'.
The perfect passive ends in bare worden, never geworden: 'ist geschrieben worden' = has been written.
er habe is Konjunktiv I for reported speech: it flags 'er habe das Geld überwiesen' as his claim, something the speaker does not vouch for.
ich wünschte signals an unreal wish and pulls the subjunctive: 'ich könnte besser singen', könnte not kann.
'wenn es nach mir ginge' is a set subjunctive idiom for 'if it were up to me', not a literal 'if it goes'.
verlassen alone means to leave or abandon, but with a reflexive it flips: 'wir verlassen uns auf' = we rely on.
immerhin points to one redeeming upside despite the rest: 'Immerhin hat er sich die Mühe gemacht' = at least he made the effort.
ja wohl adds an indignant 'surely, obviously': 'Das ist ja wohl das Mindeste' = that is surely the very least you can expect.
ja in 'Das ist ja unglaublich' stresses the fact as plain to see, a reaction, with no separate word in English.
doch mal warms a bare command into a friendly invite: 'Komm doch mal vorbei' softens 'Komm vorbei' to why don't you drop by.
